before.a: AutoGPT is one of the first open-source autonomous AI agent frameworks, released in 2023. It connects GPT-4 to tools (web search, file management, code execution) and runs in a loop to complete multi-step tasks. It's a framework for developers, not a polished consumer product.

AutoGPT pioneered the autonomous agent concept but has been surpassed by more capable agents like Manus, Devin, and Claude Code for practical use. It remains important as an open-source reference and for developers studying autonomous agent architectures.

Manus is more capable at real-world task completion — it has better web browsing, more reliable tool use, and fewer failures on complex tasks. AutoGPT was groundbreaking but often struggled to complete tasks reliably. Manus represents the current generation of more capable autonomous agents.
before.q: What can Manus do that AutoGPT can't?

before.a: AutoGPT is free and open-source. You pay for the API tokens used by the AI model (GPT-4 or other). Running it requires technical knowledge — setting up Python, API keys, and dependencies.

after.a: AutoGPT is one of the first open-source "give it a goal and let it run" autonomous AI agent projects. It has since grown into the AutoGPT Platform, a full environment for designing, running, and sharing AI agents, complete with a visual Agent Builder, an agent marketplace, and a managed cloud, rather than just a single command-line script.

Yes. AutoGPT is now shipping as the AutoGPT Platform (beta v0.6.65, June 25, 2026), with active development centered on AutoPilot/Copilot features like automatic goal decomposition, an AutoPilot context panel, global search, MCP auto-discovery, public link sharing, and native scheduling and webhook triggers, alongside a visual Agent Builder and agent marketplace.

after.q: What can the AutoGPT Platform do beyond the original AutoGPT script?
after.a: The AutoGPT Platform adds a drag-and-drop Agent Builder, an agent marketplace/store for publishing and reusing agents, 30+ integrations including Slack, Discord, and Stripe, credit-based execution billing, and AutoPilot/Copilot features such as automatic goal decomposition and native scheduling and webhook triggers. It can be self-hosted or run through the managed AutoGPT Cloud, going well beyond the original single-loop agent script.

The self-hosted open-source core of AutoGPT is MIT-licensed and free if you bring your own LLM API keys and compute, with no seat limits. AutoGPT also offers a managed cloud with Pro ($50/mo, $42.50/mo billed annually) and Max ($320/mo, $272/mo billed annually) subscriptions, plus a separate pay-as-you-go credit wallet that meters agent runs at an unpublished rate.
